b1.summary: Every run is decided by security misses (7-24 failing security tests each); every run also fails functional tests, which force reward to 0 (score.py). Misses common to all 6 runs: the workspace shell allow/deny lists (T8, real upstream code the advisory fix left open; 3 tests) and the injected directly-registered AI command (T10). The functional failure common to all 6 is 'language model requests::are sent in a trusted workspace and merge workspace request settings' (plus 'merge user-level request settings' in 6/6): the models' request gates/readers broke trusted requests. It is never the sole decider: without any functional failure each run would still be below 1.0 on security (DS 0.41/0.74/0.70, MiMo 0.11/0.26/0.33). Audits judged these functional failures genuine keep-working regressions (pinned code passes functional/02, nop 32/32), so they are fair by the 'trusted workspace behaves exactly as today' sentence, but see concerns for harness sensitivity.

b3.note: Closest run DS3: 8 security + 2 functional failing (security 19/27). No run within one test of 1.0.

b4.note: T8 shell lists (3 tests), T10 injected command and the trusted language-model functional test fail in all 6 runs; beyond that coverage varies widely (DS2 misses the canRun gate, DS1/MM1 miss the request gate, MiMo runs also miss settings/aliases/templates/skills/copilot init). MM1 and MM3 hit the 2h agent cap.

b5.fairness: READY (gate_a) — FAIRNESS.md (v4 review) ends 'GATE_A: READY / NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES'. FAIRNESS.v3-stale.md is the earlier review of the pre-revision instruction (GATE_A: NOT_READY: built-in .prompts template default suppression contradicted the 'defaults keep applying' sentence); the 2026-10-20 fairness_revision fixed it in the instruction ('A value naming a location inside the workspace is not applied...'), so the stale file is superseded history and does not matter.
b5.open_human_question: Yes, open: 'confirm that the eventless preference mutation in functional/04 and the DI stubs that omit a trust binding in security/06/09 are acceptable harness choices (they pass the primary-mechanism fix but would fail alternative, still-correct implementations)'. No record of it being answered. Relevant: security/06 'workspace-scoped extra directories' failed in all 3 MiMo runs and security/09 'provider initialisation' in 2 MiMo runs, though each of those runs has many other security misses.

b6.reason: Advisory fix e3fdfe69 (GHSA-3JWW-HXQJ-WFQ2) touches only the T1-T6 sites (file list checked on GitHub); it does not touch shell-command-permission-service, skill-service or the anthropic contribution, and never the injected ai-core-command-contribution / copilot sites. But a later upstream commit 2866ab98f (#17768, 2026-07-07, 'route AI preference reads through AiConfigurationService... centralize the trust-suppression rule') moves ShellCommandPermissionService allow/deny reads onto the trust-aware AiConfigurationService, so T8 (one of the two traps missed in every run) is visible on current upstream main. T10 (injected unwrapped command, missed in all 6 runs) and T11 are never covered upstream and survive lookup.

quotes: Every attempt to use an AI feature is refused with an error, however it is reached, and no AI feature starts or initialises on the workspace's behalf.
Whether AI is enabled is a preference; whether it may run is governed by trust.
A value naming a location inside the workspace is not applied while the workspace is untrusted
including content at a location inside the workspace that a built-in default or a user value names
Hidden checks resolve `AIActivationService` and read `isActive`, `canRun` and their change events; `canRun` is false whenever the workspace is not trusted.
Fix the flaw everywhere it can be reached, not only the example.
b7.note: No site, route, variant list or flaw count is named (the v4 upgrade removed the earlier per-setting list). The isActive/canRun split, 'starts or initialises' and the inside-workspace-default sentence point at T1/T10/T11 and T6/T7 shapes without naming them.

b8.blind: not run — no blind_status.txt and no blind patch in checks/; manifest gate.static notes the missing kind=blind pass patch
b8.note: Two alternative passing patches: pass-alt-execution.patch (different execution-gate design and trust cache) and pass-hardening.patch. Reference fix is ~1150 lines over 23 files.

c1.mechanism: trust-boundary bypass / authz: untrusted-workspace configuration and content (Restricted Mode) influencing or running AI features — config injection into tool/shell auto-approval, provider endpoints, prompts

c2.pattern: missed indirect route (unguarded config reader) + missed second copy (unwrapped sibling command)
c2.note: Common decisive misses: T8 shell allow/deny lists read raw from PreferenceService (real code, not in the advisory fix) and T10 an injected command registered without the AI wrapper and enabled on the preference-only isActive flag. Secondary common failure: over-blocked/broken trusted request path (keep-working).

d2.evidence: injection.patch adds two small sites. (1) ai-core-command-contribution.ts: a new AI_SHOW_MODEL_STATUS_COMMAND ('Show AI Model Status', codicon 'pulse') registered directly with isEnabled: () => this.activationService.isActive, beside the existing wrapped AI_SHOW_SETTINGS_COMMAND — ordinary maintainer code, no comments or odd names. Caveat: its execute only opens the preferences page at 'ai-features.models', so the injected 'hole' has negligible real security impact; it is a hole only by the instruction's 'every AI feature, however reached' rule (consistent with upstream disabling the wrapped settings command via canRun). (2) copilot-frontend-application-contribution.ts: injects AIActivationService and adds `if (!this.activationService.isActive) { return; }` at the top of initializeModels — a natural-looking guard on the wrong flag (decoy that makes the site look handled). Neither site is dead code or unnaturally duplicated.

e3.why: Gate a READY, but FAIRNESS.md leaves NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES open (harness stubs in functional/04, security/06/09), and two of those flagged tests failed in MiMo runs.

e4.why: T8 missed in all 6 runs: a workspace allowlist auto-approves shell commands / a workspace [] removes the built-in deny list while untrusted — a real security hole.

e5.why: T10 (injected, missed in all 6 runs) is never covered upstream; T8 is outside the advisory fix but later covered by upstream #17768, so only partly.

concerns: Open human-review question in FAIRNESS.md (harness stubs could fail alternative correct designs: eventless preference mutation in functional/04, no trust binding in security/06/09 containers); security/06 extra-dirs failed 3/3 MiMo, security/09 2/3 MiMo.

The same functional test (trusted LM request merging workspace settings) fails in 6/6 runs across both models. Audits call it a genuine regression and pinned code passes it, but the functional/02 container binds no ContextKeyService or AIActivationService stub (so a fix that injects AIActivationService into the LM service cannot be constructed), the PreferenceService stub is partial although the instruction says 'its public API is available', and the request is sent in the same tick as construction. Not decisive (each run also misses >=7 security tests), but rewards are 0 because of it, so margins look wider than security alone shows.
2 of 3 MiMo failures are 2h agent-cap timeouts; MM1 barely touched the trust code (security 3/27, functional 5/32), so that run says little about the traps.
T10, one of the two traps missed in every run, has negligible real impact (a command that opens a preferences page); the substantive common miss is T8.
T8 is fixed on later upstream main (#17768 AiConfigurationService), so with internet the shell trap is lookup-able; only the injected T10/T11 survive for sure.
No blind fix was run (blind_status absent).
Very broad task (11 traps, 27 security + 32 functional tests, ~1150-line reference); difficulty is partly breadth.
one_line: Theia AI workspace-trust breaker: in all six runs both models leave the workspace shell allow/deny lists (real code the advisory fix missed, later fixed upstream) and an injected unwrapped AI command open, and also break trusted language-model requests.
